problem: "Principle" is correct but empty — it doesn't tell you that 原则 lives almost entirely in a few fixed phrases about rules of conduct and negotiating positions.
meaning: The standing rule you operate by and won't bend on — in personal terms "having principles," in official terms the agreed basis for a policy or deal. Not "principle" as in a scientific law (that's 原理).
contrast: 原理 is how something works (工作原理, 杠杆原理); 原则 is what you refuse to violate. 方针 is the policy direction set from above; 原则 is the constraint the policy must respect.
collocations: 原则上 (yuánzé shàng) — in principle, in theory (often with an unspoken "but")
坚持原则 (jiānchí yuánzé) — stick to one's principles
有原则/讲原则 (yǒu/jiǎng yuánzé) — be a person of principle
原则问题 (yuánzé wèntí) — a matter of principle, non-negotiable
基本原则 (jīběn yuánzé) — fundamental principles
sentence: 原则上我同意，但具体细节还要再谈。
sentence_meaning: In principle I agree, but we still need to discuss the specifics.

problem: Four English verbs in one gloss with nothing tying them together; the sample sentence shows 主持人 (a noun) rather than the verb.
meaning: To be the one running the thing — standing at the front of a ceremony or broadcast, or being in charge of a project or department day to day. Two flavours: hosting an event, and heading up work.
contrast: 举行 is holding an event (the event happens); 主持 is a person running it. 负责 is being responsible for something; 主持 adds that you're the one directing it from the front, often temporarily or in an acting capacity (主持工作 = acting head).
collocations: 主持会议 (zhǔchí huìyì) — chair a meeting
主持婚礼/节目 (zhǔchí hūnlǐ/jiémù) — officiate a wedding / host a show
主持工作 (zhǔchí gōngzuò) — be in charge of, act as head
主持公道 (zhǔchí gōngdào) — see that justice is done
sentence: 这个项目由王教授主持，已经进行了三年。
sentence_meaning: This project is headed by Professor Wang and has been running for three years.
was: to preside over; to host; to manage; to direct

problem: Glossed "and," which makes it interchangeable with 和 / 与 / 还有 in your head — it isn't; it has a specific position and a hierarchy to it.
meaning: A written "and" that joins the last item onto a list, typically after commas or 、, and often after the heavier items — the tail of an enumeration. It can also link whole phrases and clauses, which 和 does badly.
contrast: 和 joins two nouns casually and can't easily end a long list or link verb phrases. 与 is 和's formal twin, used in titles and pairings (中国与世界). 及 is 以及 compressed, even more written. 还有 is spoken. Rough feel: the things after 以及 are secondary or an add-on to what came before.
collocations: ……、……以及…… — the standard end-of-list slot
以及其他 (yǐjí qítā) — as well as others
以及如何…… (yǐjí rúhé) — and also how to…
sentence: 会议讨论了预算、人事安排以及明年的发展方向。
sentence_meaning: The meeting discussed the budget, staffing arrangements, and next year's direction of development.

problem: "However/but" puts it in a pile with 但是, 可是, 不过, 却 with no way to tell them apart.
meaning: Written "however." It starts a new sentence (or follows a full stop or semicolon) and reverses the direction of what you just said — the turn is stated as a fact, often with a note of regret or irony.
contrast: 但是 works in the same sentence right after a comma and is neutral in register; 然而 prefers to begin a fresh sentence and sounds essayistic. 不过 is light and spoken ("though"). 却 sits after the subject inside the clause, not at the front. If you'd write it in an editorial, 然而; if you'd say it out loud, 但是/不过.
collocations: 然而，事实并非如此 (rán'ér, shìshí bìngfēi rúcǐ) — however, that is not the case
然而事与愿违 (rán'ér shì yǔ yuàn wéi) — however, things turned out contrary to hopes
……。然而，…… — sentence-initial pivot in writing
sentence: 大家都以为他会放弃。然而，他坚持到了最后。
sentence_meaning: Everyone assumed he would give up. He kept going to the end, however.

problem: "Belong to" makes you think of possession, so you miss its most common use: sorting something into a category.
meaning: X 属于 Y = X falls under Y, X counts as a Y. It's mostly classification (this counts as that kind of thing); ownership is a secondary use, and there's a warm idiomatic use for "this moment is ours."
contrast: 是 equates; 属于 places into a larger set, so Y is always the bigger category. 归 / 归……所有 is the legal-ownership word.
collocations: 属于……范围/范畴 (shǔyú… fànwéi/fànchóu) — falls within the scope/category of
属于个人行为 (shǔyú gèrén xíngwéi) — counts as a personal act
这属于什么情况 (zhè shǔyú shénme qíngkuàng) — what category of situation is this
属于我们的时代 (shǔyú wǒmen de shídài) — an era that belongs to us
sentence: 迟到十分钟属于小问题，可以补救。
sentence_meaning: Being ten minutes late counts as a minor issue and can be fixed.
was: to belong to; to be part of

problem: "Besides / in addition" is shared with 另外, 而且, 再者, 加上 — the gloss can't pick it out.
meaning: Written "apart from this / in addition." It opens a new sentence to add a further point after you've finished the previous one, typically the second or third item in a written argument, report, or list of reasons.
contrast: 另外 does the same job but is fine in speech and can also mean "a different one." 而且 attaches inside the same sentence to intensify ("and what's more"), it can't start a fresh paragraph the way 此外 does. 再说 is spoken-casual. 此外 is cool and list-like: point one, point two.
collocations: 此外，还有…… (cǐwài, hái yǒu) — in addition, there is also…
除此之外 (chú cǐ zhī wài) — apart from this (the longer form)
此外无他 (cǐwài wú tā) — nothing else besides
sentence: 这份工作要求有三年经验；此外，还需要熟练使用英语。
sentence_meaning: This job requires three years of experience; in addition, fluent English is needed.

problem: Four glosses spanning "approve" to "ratify" blur the core idea: it's about being acknowledged as good enough, not about granting permission.
meaning: To acknowledge that something or someone measures up — the nod of recognition from peers, the public, or an authority. Very often used as a noun: 得到认可 = to gain recognition.
contrast: 批准 is official permission to proceed (a form gets stamped). 承认 is admitting a fact, including unpleasant ones. 认可 is judging something acceptable/worthy, and carries approval of quality.
collocations: 得到认可 (dédào rènkě) — gain recognition/acceptance
广泛认可 (guǎngfàn rènkě) — widely recognised
认可度 (rènkě dù) — level of acceptance, how well received something is
不被认可 (bù bèi rènkě) — not recognised (e.g. a qualification)
sentence: 这所大学的学历在国外也得到认可。
sentence_meaning: This university's degrees are recognised abroad as well.
was: to approve; to accept; to recognize; to ratify

problem: "Original; primitive" reads as two unrelated words, so you guess wrong half the time; the sample only shows the "primitive" side.
meaning: Two linked senses: the raw, as-first-recorded version of something (原始数据 = the raw data before anyone processed it), and primitive as in early-stage humanity or crudely undeveloped. Same idea both times — before anything was done to it.
contrast: 原来 is "originally / it turns out." 本来 is "originally, by rights." 最初 is "at first" in time. 原始 is an adjective attached to a noun: the original copy, the raw file, primitive society.
collocations: 原始数据/文件 (yuánshǐ shùjù/wénjiàn) — raw data, original file
原始社会 (yuánshǐ shèhuì) — primitive society
原始森林 (yuánshǐ sēnlín) — old-growth/virgin forest
原始积累 (yuánshǐ jīlěi) — primitive accumulation (of capital)
sentence: 请把原始数据保存好，不要直接在上面修改。
sentence_meaning: Please keep the raw data safe; don't edit it directly.

problem: "Domain; sphere; field; area" — four near-synonyms, none showing that 领域 is the standard word for a field of work or research and is almost always modified.
meaning: A field of activity or expertise — science, education, AI, the arts. It nearly always comes with a modifier in front (X 领域) and pairs with words like 专家, 研究, 应用.
contrast: 方面 is "aspect/respect" of a topic, much lighter. 范围 is the extent or scope of something (how far it reaches). 行业 is an industry in the commercial sense. 领域 is the intellectual or professional terrain.
collocations: 在……领域 (zài… lǐngyù) — in the field of…
研究领域 (yánjiū lǐngyù) — research field
各个领域 (gègè lǐngyù) — every field, across the board
领先领域 / 前沿领域 (qiányán lǐngyù) — cutting-edge field
sentence: 人工智能已经应用到医疗、教育等多个领域。
sentence_meaning: AI has already been applied in many fields, including medicine and education.

problem: "And then / thus" collapses it into 从而 and 因此, which is exactly the confusion; the difference is escalation, not result.
meaning: "And going on from there" — you did step one, and it lets you move up to a further, bigger step. It sits before the second verb phrase, usually with the same subject, and the second step is a deepening of the first.
contrast: 从而 marks a result or consequence (B happens because of A). 进而 marks a next stage you then proceed to (A first, then push on to B). 因此 just states a reason-result link. Test: if B is something you go on to do, 进而; if B is what A brought about, 从而.
collocations: 先……进而…… (xiān… jìn'ér…) — first…, and then go on to…
进而影响 (jìn'ér yǐngxiǎng) — and thereby go on to affect
进而推动 (jìn'ér tuīdòng) — and further drive/promote
sentence: 研究先分析了病因，进而提出了新的治疗方案。
sentence_meaning: The study first analysed the causes of the disease, and went on from there to propose a new treatment.
was: and then; thereby going on to; and thus proceed to

problem: "Dialect" is a one-to-one translation, so the card gives you nothing to grip; you fail it because it's stored as an English word, not a Chinese one.
meaning: A regional variety of Chinese — Cantonese, Shanghainese, Sichuanese. In practice it's the word for "the way people talk back home," set against 普通话.
contrast: 口音 is an accent — the same language pronounced differently. 方言 is a whole regional variety with its own vocabulary, often mutually unintelligible.
collocations: 说方言 (shuō fāngyán) — speak dialect
地方方言 / 各地方言 (gèdì fāngyán) — local dialects
方言区 (fāngyán qū) — dialect region
保护方言 (bǎohù fāngyán) — preserve dialects
sentence: 年轻一代大多讲普通话，会说方言的越来越少。
sentence_meaning: The younger generation mostly speaks Mandarin; fewer and fewer can speak the dialect.

problem: The gloss lists two uses, but 达成 is really a narrow collocation word — it takes a very small set of objects, and that's what should be memorised.
meaning: To arrive at something jointly after a process — an agreement, a consensus, a deal. Think of it as the verb that goes with 协议 and 共识 more than as a general "achieve."
contrast: 实现 is realising a goal or dream. 完成 is finishing a task. 达到 is reaching a level or standard (达到标准, 达到目的). 达成 is nearly always two parties arriving at terms.
collocations: 达成协议 (dáchéng xiéyì) — reach an agreement
达成共识 (dáchéng gòngshí) — reach a consensus
达成一致 (dáchéng yīzhì) — come to agreement
达成合作/交易 (dáchéng hézuò/jiāoyì) — conclude a partnership/deal
sentence: 经过三轮谈判，双方终于达成了共识。
sentence_meaning: After three rounds of negotiation, the two sides finally reached a consensus.

problem: "Always" invites confusion with 总是 and 从来, and misses that 一向 describes a settled, known trait over a long stretch of past time.
meaning: "Has always been that way" — describes someone's long-standing habit or character up to now, with a slight sense that this is common knowledge. Goes before the adjective or verb.
contrast: 总是 = habitually, often with complaint, any time frame. 从来 needs a negative or 都 and means "never/ever, at any point." 一直 is continuous over a specific stretch (可以是最近). 一向 is the settled reputation: 他一向如此 — he's always been like this.
collocations: 一向如此 (yīxiàng rúcǐ) — has always been this way
一向不……(yīxiàng bù) — has never been one to…
身体一向很好 (shēntǐ yīxiàng hěn hǎo) — has always been in good health
sentence: 他一向不喜欢跟人争，这次却发了脾气。
sentence_meaning: He's never been one to argue with people, but this time he lost his temper.
was: all along; the whole time; consistently; always

problem: "Justice; righteousness" is abstract-to-abstract; nothing tells you 正义 is mostly used as a modifier and in moral rather than legal-procedural contexts.
meaning: Justice in the moral sense — the right side, what is just. Used as a noun (伸张正义) and very commonly as an adjective in front of a noun: a just cause, a just war.
contrast: 公正 is fairness/impartiality in how someone is treated or judged — that's the procedural word (公正的判决). 司法公正 for court fairness; 正义 for the moral cause. 公平 is fairness in distribution.
collocations: 伸张正义 (shēnzhāng zhèngyì) — uphold/see justice done
正义感 (zhèngyì gǎn) — a sense of justice
正义的事业/战争 (zhèngyì de shìyè) — a just cause / just war
主持正义 (zhǔchí zhèngyì) — stand up for what's right
sentence: 他这个人很有正义感，看不惯别人受欺负。
sentence_meaning: He has a strong sense of justice and can't stand seeing others bullied.

problem: "Thus; thereby" is the same gloss as 因此 and 进而, which is why it keeps slipping.
meaning: Written "and thereby" — the first clause is a measure taken, the second is the good result it produces. It sits at the head of the second clause, with no new subject, and the two halves are one sentence.
contrast: 因此 can start a fresh sentence and explains a cause-effect for anything, including bad outcomes. 进而 means going on to a further step, not producing a result. 从而 specifically frames B as the payoff of doing A — the standard sentence of reports and proposals: 采取了X，从而Y了。
collocations: ……，从而提高了…… (cóng'ér tígāo le) — thereby raising…
从而实现 (cóng'ér shíxiàn) — thereby achieving
从而避免 (cóng'ér bìmiǎn) — thereby avoiding
sentence: 公司简化了审批流程，从而降低了运营成本。
sentence_meaning: The company simplified its approval process, thereby lowering operating costs.

problem: "Formulate; draw up" is right but doesn't tell you the restricted set of objects — 制定 lives or dies by what follows it.
meaning: To draw up something official and rule-like: laws, policies, standards, plans. The subject is normally an institution or a team, not a private individual doodling.
contrast: 制作 is making a physical thing or a video. 规定 is stipulating a rule (and as a noun, the rule itself). 拟定 is drafting a preliminary version. 制订 is a near-twin used for plans still open to revision; 制定 implies it's finalised and in force.
collocations: 制定法律/政策 (zhìdìng fǎlǜ/zhèngcè) — enact laws / formulate policy
制定计划 (zhìdìng jìhuà) — draw up a plan
制定标准 (zhìdìng biāozhǔn) — set standards
制定规则 (zhìdìng guīzé) — lay down the rules
sentence: 政府正在制定新的环保政策。
sentence_meaning: The government is drawing up new environmental policies.
was: to formulate; to draw up; to lay down (a plan or policy)

problem: "Establish; found" misses half the word — the very common second sense, that an argument or charge holds up.
meaning: Two senses. One: an organisation comes into being / is founded (often intransitive — 公司成立于1998年, no object needed). Two: a claim, theory, or accusation stands up, is valid — 这个说法不成立.
contrast: 建立 is establishing relations, systems, trust — it always takes an object and doesn't mean "be valid." 创立 is founding something new from scratch, with a founder in view. 设立 is setting up a post, fund, or branch office.
collocations: 成立于……年 (chénglì yú) — founded in the year…
宣布成立 (xuānbù chénglì) — announce the establishment of
不成立 (bù chénglì) — doesn't hold, invalid
理由不成立 (lǐyóu bù chénglì) — the reason doesn't stand up
sentence: 如果这个前提不成立，后面的结论也就没有意义了。
sentence_meaning: If this premise doesn't hold, the conclusions that follow are meaningless too.
was: to establish; to found; to set up

problem: "Hold (a meeting)" overlaps with 开, 召开, 举办 and gives no way to choose; the card also doesn't show its favourite passive-ish pattern.
meaning: To hold a formal event — ceremonies, games, elections, talks. Most often the event is the subject and 举行 comes at the end: 奥运会在北京举行.
contrast: 举办 focuses on the organiser putting the event on (举办展览, 举办比赛) and takes a doer. 召开 is specifically convening a meeting or congress. 开会 is the plain spoken version. 举行 leans towards ceremonies and scheduled occasions, and often appears with 在…举行.
collocations: 举行婚礼/葬礼 (jǔxíng hūnlǐ/zànglǐ) — hold a wedding/funeral
举行会谈 (jǔxíng huìtán) — hold talks
举行仪式 (jǔxíng yíshì) — hold a ceremony
如期举行 (rúqī jǔxíng) — take place as scheduled
sentence: 开幕仪式将于下周五在体育馆举行。
sentence_meaning: The opening ceremony will be held next Friday at the gymnasium.
was: convene; to hold (a meeting, ceremony, etc.)

problem: Listing "structure" first is misleading — in everyday modern use it almost always means an organisation/agency, and it's the standard word for formal bodies.
meaning: An institution or agency — a formally constituted body with a function: a government agency, a research institute, a bank, a tutoring company. Also, in a bureaucratic sense, the apparatus/setup of an organisation (机构改革, 精简机构).
contrast: 组织 is an organisation as a group of people, and also the verb "to organise." 单位 is your workplace, especially a state one. 部门 is a department inside a larger body. 机构 is the entity as an official institution seen from the outside — and in finance, 机构 means institutional investors.
collocations: 金融机构 (jīnróng jīgòu) — financial institution
政府机构 (zhèngfǔ jīgòu) — government agency
培训机构 (péixùn jīgòu) — training/tutoring company
医疗机构 (yīliáo jīgòu) — medical institution
sentence: 这项调查由一家独立研究机构完成。
sentence_meaning: This survey was carried out by an independent research institution.

problem: "Comfort; console" is fine for the verb, but the card hides that 安慰 is just as often an adjective/noun — "a comfort," "feel comforted" — and the sample sentence is odd.
meaning: To console someone who's upset, with words. Equally common as a state or a thing: 心里得到安慰 (feel comforted), 是一种安慰 (it's some consolation), 感到安慰 (be reassured/gratified).
contrast: 鼓励 is urging someone on towards something. 劝 is talking someone into or out of an action. 安慰 only tries to make the hurt easier to bear; it doesn't ask for anything.
collocations: 安慰她几句 (ānwèi tā jǐ jù) — say a few comforting words to her
感到安慰 (gǎndào ānwèi) — feel comforted / be gratified
是个安慰 (shì ge ānwèi) — is some consolation
安慰奖 (ānwèi jiǎng) — consolation prize
sentence: 孩子们都很懂事，这让她感到很安慰。
sentence_meaning: The children are all so sensible, which is a great comfort to her.

problem: The card stacks three English words together, so nothing sticks; the core of it is physical structures/architecture, and the 'to construct' use is rare in modern speech.
meaning: Buildings as physical things, and the field of architecture. Modern usage is overwhelmingly nominal: 建筑物 a structure, 建筑师 an architect, 古建筑 old buildings.
contrast: 建设 is building up something abstract or large-scale (经济建设, 城市建设); 建立 is establishing a system, relationship or organization. 建筑 is bricks and design.
collocations: 建筑师 (jiànzhùshī) — architect
古建筑 (gǔ jiànzhù) — historic buildings
建筑工地 (jiànzhù gōngdì) — construction site
建筑风格 (jiànzhù fēnggé) — architectural style
sentence: 这座教堂是城里最有名的建筑。
sentence_meaning: This church is the most famous building in the city.

problem: 'Chairperson; president' collides with 总统, 主任, 董事长 in his head, and the sentence 他是我们的主席 gives no institutional context.
meaning: The person who chairs a body — a committee, a union, an association, a meeting. It's also the title of the PRC head of state (国家主席) and the honorific in 毛主席.
contrast: 总统 is the president of a republic (US, France); 董事长 chairs a company board; 主任 heads an office or department. 主席 presides over a council or organization.
collocations: 国家主席 (guójiā zhǔxí) — state president (PRC)
主席台 (zhǔxítái) — the platform where officials sit
工会主席 (gōnghuì zhǔxí) — union chairman
担任主席 (dānrèn zhǔxí) — serve as chair
sentence: 会议由协会主席主持。
sentence_meaning: The meeting was chaired by the president of the association.

problem: 'Summarize' is misleading — that's 总结. 综合 is about merging several separate things, not boiling something down.
meaning: To put several separate factors together and treat them as one; as a modifier, 'combined, all-round, general-purpose'. Think 综合考虑 — weigh everything together before deciding.
contrast: 总结 = sum up experience or lessons afterwards. 全面 = covering every side (comprehensive in coverage). 综合 = the act of combining multiple inputs.
collocations: 综合考虑 (zōnghé kǎolǜ) — take everything into account
综合实力 (zōnghé shílì) — overall strength
综合大学 (zōnghé dàxué) — comprehensive university
综合素质 (zōnghé sùzhì) — all-round quality/ability
sentence: 综合各方面的情况来看，这个方案更可行。
sentence_meaning: Taking all the circumstances together, this plan is more workable.

problem: 'Implement / carry out' is exactly the gloss he has on 进行, 执行 and 落实, so the card can't be told apart from those.
meaning: Formal, official word for putting a law, policy, regulation or plan into force. Its subject is usually a government or institution, and it's the verb you see in news and legal text.
contrast: 执行 = carry out an order, task or sentence (enforce what's been decided); 落实 = make sure it actually gets done on the ground; 进行 = the neutral 'conduct/be underway' with almost any activity. 实施 is specifically bringing rules into effect.
collocations: 实施新政策 (shíshī xīn zhèngcè) — implement a new policy
正式实施 (zhèngshì shíshī) — formally take effect
实施方案 (shíshī fāng'àn) — implementation plan
分阶段实施 (fēn jiēduàn shíshī) — implement in stages
sentence: 新的交通法规将从下月一日起实施。
sentence_meaning: The new traffic regulations will take effect on the first of next month.
was: to implement; put into effect; carry out

problem: 'Stable; steady' is right but hookless, and the card ignores that 稳定 is also a verb ('stabilize') and a noun in formal writing.
meaning: Not fluctuating — prices, jobs, health, a society, a person's mood. Also used transitively: 稳定物价 hold prices steady, 稳定情绪 calm someone down.
contrast: 固定 is fixed in place or fixed in amount (固定工资); 安定 is a settled, peaceful life or social order; 稳定 is the absence of ups and downs.
collocations: 工作稳定 (gōngzuò wěndìng) — a secure job
物价稳定 (wùjià wěndìng) — stable prices
稳定发展 (wěndìng fāzhǎn) — steady development
稳定情绪 (wěndìng qíngxù) — calm someone's emotions
sentence: 病人的情况已经稳定下来了。
sentence_meaning: The patient's condition has stabilized.

problem: 'Take/adopt' overlaps with 采用 and 采纳; and the old sentence (人民采取激烈的抗议行动) is stiff and unidiomatic.
meaning: To adopt a course of action — it takes a short list of abstract objects: 措施, 行动, 政策, 态度, 手段, 方式, 立场. Almost formulaic in news and official language.
contrast: 采用 = put a method, technology or material to use (采用新技术); 采纳 = accept someone's suggestion or opinion (采纳建议). 采取 is about the stance or measures you take.
collocations: 采取措施 (cǎiqǔ cuòshī) — take measures
采取行动 (cǎiqǔ xíngdòng) — take action
采取强硬态度 (cǎiqǔ qiángyìng tàidù) — take a hard line
采取有效手段 (cǎiqǔ yǒuxiào shǒuduàn) — use effective means
sentence: 政府采取了一系列措施控制房价。
sentence_meaning: The government took a series of measures to control housing prices.
was: carry out or adopt; take(measures, policies, attitudes, etc.)

problem: Listing 'realize' first is misleading — 意识 alone is a noun; the verb is 意识到 and it needs the 到.
meaning: Consciousness in the medical sense (失去意识), and 'awareness' of some issue — 环保意识, 安全意识, 法律意识. To say 'realize', you need 意识到 + a clause.
contrast: 认识 is understanding or knowledge of something (对问题的认识); 意识 is either being conscious or having an internalized awareness. 意识到 = the moment of realizing.
collocations: 失去意识 (shīqù yìshí) — lose consciousness
安全意识 (ānquán yìshí) — safety awareness
环保意识 (huánbǎo yìshí) — environmental awareness
意识到 (yìshí dào) — to realize that…
sentence: 他这才意识到自己犯了个大错。
sentence_meaning: Only then did he realize he'd made a big mistake.

problem: It isn't a standalone word — asking for its meaning alone is asking for something that never occurs in speech.
meaning: Background sense: to unfold, stretch out, loosen up — hence 'at ease, comfortable' inside compounds. Also a surname and a transliteration syllable (舒伯特 Schubert).
collocations: 舒服 (shūfu) — comfortable, feeling well
舒适 (shūshì) — comfortable (written, of places/conditions)
舒缓 (shūhuǎn) — gentle, slow-paced; to ease
舒展 (shūzhǎn) — to stretch out, unfurl
sentence: 这几天睡得不好，身上不太舒服。
sentence_meaning: I haven't slept well these last few days and don't feel great.

problem: The gloss 'underwear' is wrong — that's 内衣. 衬 is a lining, and it never stands alone.
meaning: Background sense: the layer underneath — a lining, or by extension setting something off against a background. That's why it gives 衬衫 (shirt, originally the under-garment) and 衬托 (to set off).
collocations: 衬衫 (chènshān) — shirt
衬衣 (chènyī) — shirt, undershirt
衬托 (chèntuō) — to set off, provide a foil for
陪衬 (péichèn) — serve as a foil/backdrop
sentence: 他穿了一件白衬衫，配了条深色领带。
sentence_meaning: He wore a white shirt with a dark tie.

problem: 'Achievement' is correct but sits in a pile with 成绩, 成果, 成功 — nothing marks out which one 成就 is.
meaning: A major accomplishment, usually career- or lifetime-scale, something you're credited with. Standard verb is 取得; 有成就 means being accomplished, and 成就感 is the feeling of accomplishment.
contrast: 成绩 = results/marks, smaller and measurable (考试成绩); 成果 = the concrete fruits of work, esp. research (研究成果); 成功 = success as a state. 成就 is the big, honorable achievement.
collocations: 取得成就 (qǔdé chéngjiù) — achieve accomplishments
成就感 (chéngjiùgǎn) — sense of achievement
伟大的成就 (wěidà de chéngjiù) — great achievement
毕生成就奖 (bìshēng chéngjiù jiǎng) — lifetime achievement award
sentence: 他在医学研究上取得了很大的成就。
sentence_meaning: He has made great achievements in medical research.

problem: 'Violate (a law)' is too narrow and blurs into 违法 and 违背.
meaning: To break a written rule — 规定, 法律, 纪律, 合同, 规则. It always takes an object.
contrast: 违法 is a verb-object unit meaning 'break the law' and takes no object after it (他违法了); 违背 goes against something non-written — a promise, principle, one's conscience or someone's wishes (违背承诺). 违反 = breach a stated rule.
collocations: 违反规定 (wéifǎn guīdìng) — violate the rules
违反纪律 (wéifǎn jìlǜ) — breach discipline
违反交通规则 (wéifǎn jiāotōng guīzé) — break traffic rules
严重违反 (yánzhòng wéifǎn) — seriously violate
sentence: 他因违反公司规定被开除了。
sentence_meaning: He was fired for violating company rules.

problem: 'Carry on / undertake' says nothing about the one thing that matters: 进行 is a light verb that carries a two-syllable activity noun, and he confuses it with 实施 and 举行.
meaning: The all-purpose formal verb for 'conduct/carry out'. It props up a two-syllable abstract activity — 进行讨论/调查/谈判/改革/比较 — and turns it into a proper predicate. Also 正在进行中 'underway'.
contrast: 实施 is only for laws, policies and plans taking effect; 举行/举办 are for events and ceremonies (举行婚礼); 开展 is for launching a campaign or drive. 进行 is the neutral default and the most colorless of them.
collocations: 进行讨论 (jìnxíng tǎolùn) — hold a discussion
进行调查 (jìnxíng diàochá) — conduct an investigation
顺利进行 (shùnlì jìnxíng) — proceed smoothly
正在进行中 (zhèngzài jìnxíng zhōng) — in progress
sentence: 双方就贸易问题进行了三轮谈判。
sentence_meaning: The two sides held three rounds of talks on trade issues.
was: to carry on; carry out; undertake

problem: Glossed the same as 一定, 肯定, 必定 and 难免, so the card can't be distinguished from any of them.
meaning: 'Inevitably, as a matter of course' — a written, argumentative word claiming something follows by necessity. Sits before the verb (必然会…), and also works as a modifier or noun: 必然结果, 必然趋势, 历史的必然.
contrast: 一定 and 肯定 are everyday confidence about a fact ('surely, definitely') and 一定 also expresses insistence (你一定要来); 必定 is close to 必然 but purely adverbial; 难免 means 'hard to avoid' with a negative flavor. 必然 = objective logical or historical necessity, essay register.
collocations: 必然结果 (bìrán jiéguǒ) — inevitable result
必然趋势 (bìrán qūshì) — inevitable trend
必然会 (bìrán huì) — is bound to
历史的必然 (lìshǐ de bìrán) — a historical inevitability
sentence: 技术落后必然导致竞争力下降。
sentence_meaning: Falling behind technologically inevitably leads to a loss of competitiveness.

problem: Two unrelated jobs are crammed into one gloss with four synonyms, and the sample sentence uses both at once, which just muddles them.
meaning: As a degree adverb before adjectives, 'quite/considerably' — noticeably stronger than 比较, a bit below 非常, and slightly formal. Separately, 相当（于）means 'equal to / on a par with': 两人水平相当, 一英里相当于1.6公里.
contrast: 比较 is mild ('relatively'); 非常/十分 are strong; 挺 is casual speech. 相当 leans written and is used with adjectives, not bare verbs.
collocations: 相当复杂 (xiāngdāng fùzá) — quite complicated
相当不错 (xiāngdāng bùcuò) — pretty good
相当于 (xiāngdāng yú) — equivalent to
实力相当 (shílì xiāngdāng) — evenly matched
sentence: 这份报告写得相当详细。
sentence_meaning: This report is written in considerable detail.
was: (adverb) quite; fairly; considerably; (verb) to be equal to; to match

problem: Nothing wrong with the gloss — it fails because it's stored as a bare English word with no phrases attached.
meaning: An ad, in any medium. Note the verbs that go with it: 登广告 place an ad (in print), 打广告 run advertising, 做广告 advertise / appear in an ad.
contrast: 宣传 is publicity or promotion in general (including propaganda); 广告 is the paid ad itself.
collocations: 登广告 (dēng guǎnggào) — place an advertisement
打广告 (dǎ guǎnggào) — run ads
广告公司 (guǎnggào gōngsī) — ad agency
广告牌 (guǎnggàopái) — billboard
sentence: 这个牌子请了明星来拍广告。
sentence_meaning: This brand hired a celebrity to shoot a commercial.

problem: 'To run; operate' is the same gloss he has on 运转, 操作 and 经营, with nothing marking what kind of subject 运行 takes.
meaning: Used of machines, systems, software, trains and planets — something moving along its intended course. Its subject is the system itself, not a person.
contrast: 运转 emphasizes turning/functioning (of machinery, or an organization's workings); 操作 is a person operating equipment; 经营 is running a business; 行驶 is a vehicle moving on a road. 运行 = the system is up and going.
collocations: 正常运行 (zhèngcháng yùnxíng) — run normally
系统运行 (xìtǒng yùnxíng) — the system runs
运行速度 (yùnxíng sùdù) — running speed
列车运行图 (lièchē yùnxíngtú) — train timetable/diagram
sentence: 这套软件在旧电脑上也能正常运行。
sentence_meaning: This software runs fine even on old computers.
was: to run; to operate; to be in motion

problem: 'Agree with; approve of' makes it look like a synonym of 同意, and hides the identity sense that's half its usage.
meaning: To accept something as right and feel aligned with it — a view, a value, a way of doing things. As a noun it's 'identity/identification': 身份认同, 文化认同.
contrast: 同意 is agreeing to a specific proposal or request (同意我去); 赞同 is endorsing an opinion; 认同 is deeper buy-in or a sense of belonging, and works as a noun, which 同意 doesn't.
collocations: 文化认同 (wénhuà rèntóng) — cultural identity
身份认同 (shēnfèn rèntóng) — sense of identity
得到认同 (dédào rèntóng) — win acceptance/recognition
不认同这种做法 (bù rèntóng zhè zhǒng zuòfǎ) — don't endorse this approach
sentence: 很多年轻员工并不认同公司的这套价值观。
sentence_meaning: A lot of the younger employees simply don't buy into the company's values.
was: to identify with; to agree with; to approve of

problem: 'Come from' is the gloss on 来自 and 源于 too, so the card gives him no way to pick 出自.
meaning: Written verb for tracing a work, quote or product back to its source — a book, an author, a workshop, a school. Followed directly by the source, no preposition.
contrast: 来自 = comes from a place or origin generally (他来自广东); 出于 = out of a motive (出于好奇); 源于 = has its roots/origin in (这个词源于拉丁语). 出自 = 'is by / is taken from' a specific source.
collocations: 出自名家之手 (chūzì míngjiā zhī shǒu) — by a master's hand
这句话出自《论语》 (…chūzì Lúnyǔ) — this line is from the Analects
出自同一家工厂 (chūzì tóng yī jiā gōngchǎng) — from the same factory
出自本人意愿 (chūzì běnrén yìyuàn) — of one's own free will
sentence: 这段台词出自一部老电影。
sentence_meaning: This line comes from an old film.
was: to come from; to originate from

problem: 'Similar; alike' doesn't separate it from 类似 and 相同, and gives him no sense of how it's built into a sentence.
meaning: Two things resemble each other. It's a predicate: A 跟 B 相似, or 两者很相似. Nouns from it: 相似之处 points of similarity, 相似度 degree of similarity.
contrast: 相同 = identical/the same; 类似 mostly sits before a noun or takes 于 (类似的情况, 类似于); 像 is the spoken option. 相似 is the neutral written 'resemble each other'.
collocations: 非常相似 (fēicháng xiāngsì) — very similar
相似之处 (xiāngsì zhī chù) — similarities
跟…相似 (gēn… xiāngsì) — similar to…
相似度 (xiāngsìdù) — similarity (degree)
sentence: 这两款手机外观相似，性能却差别很大。
sentence_meaning: These two phones look alike, but their performance is very different.

problem: 'Obtain; acquire; gain' is exactly what his 得到 and 取得 cards say, so there's nothing to choose between them.
meaning: Formal 'to receive/win' — what you get after effort or by award: prizes, titles, degrees, approval, support, freedom. Very common in news and résumés.
contrast: 得到 is the neutral, everyday version and covers almost anything; 取得 pairs with results and progress (取得成绩/进展/胜利/联系); 收到 is physically receiving something sent. 获得 leans toward being awarded or granted.
collocations: 获得冠军 (huòdé guànjūn) — win the championship
获得支持 (huòdé zhīchí) — win support
获得批准 (huòdé pīzhǔn) — receive approval
获得学位 (huòdé xuéwèi) — obtain a degree
sentence: 她的论文获得了今年的一等奖。
sentence_meaning: Her paper won this year's first prize.

problem: The gloss stacks three English words (game/play/recreation) so nothing specific comes back; in practice 游戏 is one narrow thing — a game you play, above all a video game.
meaning: A game — nowadays first and foremost a video game (打游戏/玩游戏), otherwise a structured game with rules. In formal writing it also shows up figuratively for anything played by rules or not taken seriously.
contrast: 比赛 is a competitive match with a winner; 玩 is the verb 'to play' generally. 游戏 is the thing being played, not the event or the activity.
collocations: 电子游戏 (diànzǐ yóuxì) — video game
游戏规则 (yóuxì guīzé) — the rules of the game, also figurative
文字游戏 (wénzì yóuxì) — word games, playing with wording to dodge an issue
sentence: 他这是在玩文字游戏，根本没回答问题。
sentence_meaning: He's just playing word games — he didn't actually answer the question.

problem: Glossed as three near-identical English verbs, so it never sticks to a use; the important half — 选择 as a noun, 'a choice' — is missing entirely.
meaning: To choose between options, and equally often the noun 'choice/option'. It's the abstract act of deciding among alternatives, which is why it fits things like career, path, life partner.
contrast: 挑 is picking through goods with your hands and eyes; 选 alone leans toward voting/selecting a person or item; 选择 is the deliberate weighing of options and the only one that works as an abstract noun.
collocations: 别无选择 (bié wú xuǎnzé) — have no other choice
做出选择 (zuòchū xuǎnzé) — make a choice
选择性 (xuǎnzéxìng) — selective, as in 选择性失明
sentence: 摆在他面前的只有两条路，他必须做出选择。
sentence_meaning: Only two roads lay before him; he had to make a choice.

problem: 'Achieve/implement/realize' pulls it toward 完成 and 达到; the card doesn't say what kind of object it takes, which is the whole trick.
meaning: To make something abstract actually come true — a dream, a goal, a promise, a plan. The thing realized is always something previously only imagined or stated.
contrast: 完成 finishes a concrete task; 达到 reaches a level or number (达到标准); 落实 puts a policy into practice on the ground. 实现 is 'it went from wish to reality'.
collocations: 实现梦想 (shíxiàn mèngxiǎng) — realize a dream
实现目标 (shíxiàn mùbiāo) — achieve a goal
自我实现 (zìwǒ shíxiàn) — self-actualization
sentence: 经过十年努力，他终于实现了当初的承诺。
sentence_meaning: After ten years of effort, he finally made good on the promise he'd made back then.

problem: 'Engineering' as a field and 'an engineering project' are two different things and the card leaves them mixed; the everyday sense is the second one.
meaning: A large construction or technical project — the thing being built, with its schedule and budget. As a modifier it means the engineering field: 工程师, 工程学.
contrast: 项目 is any project including business ones; 建筑 is the building itself. 工程 implies scale and construction/technical work — you'd never call a small office task 工程.
collocations: 工程师 (gōngchéngshī) — engineer
希望工程 (Xīwàng Gōngchéng) — the Project Hope charity scheme
豆腐渣工程 (dòufuzhā gōngchéng) — a shoddily built project
sentence: 这项工程投资巨大，工期长达五年。
sentence_meaning: This project involves enormous investment, with a construction period of five years.

problem: 'Plan/program/proposal' collides head-on with 计划 and 方法; nothing tells you 方案 is the written, worked-out version you put on the table.
meaning: A concrete worked-out proposal — a design, a scheme, a course of action written up in enough detail that people can approve or reject it. Typically one of several on offer.
contrast: 计划 is a plan over time (what you'll do when); 方法 is a method or technique; 政策 is policy. 方案 is a specific document/scheme, so it's countable: 两个方案, 备选方案.
collocations: 解决方案 (jiějué fāng'àn) — solution (esp. in business/tech)
设计方案 (shèjì fāng'àn) — design proposal
实施方案 (shíshī fāng'àn) — implementation plan
sentence: 会上提出了三个方案，最后选了成本最低的那个。
sentence_meaning: Three proposals were put forward at the meeting, and in the end they chose the cheapest one.

problem: 'To swash, surge, dash' is a dictionary entry for a bound character — 激 isn't a standalone word in modern Chinese, so there's nothing to recall. The current sentence uses a rare colloquial 激 (goad someone) that's misleading as the core meaning.
meaning: Background sense: water dashing against something and churning up — hence 'to stir up, to rouse, intense'. It only lives inside compounds, where it adds the flavour of being stirred up or violent.
collocations: 激动 (jīdòng) — worked up, emotionally stirred
刺激 (cìjī) — to stimulate/provoke; a stimulus
激烈 (jīliè) — fierce, intense (competition, argument)
激发 (jīfā) — to spark, arouse (interest, potential)
sentence: 比赛进行得非常激烈，观众都激动得站了起来。
sentence_meaning: The match was fiercely contested, and the spectators got so worked up they stood up.
was: To swash, surge, dash; To dash, excite

problem: Three glosses — technology, technique, skill — that point at three different Chinese words; the card never says which corner 技术 owns.
meaning: Technical know-how: either technology in the industrial sense, or a person's hands-on skill at doing something practical (driving, surgery, cooking).
contrast: 科技 is science-and-technology as a broad domain (科技公司, 科技新闻); 技能 is a trainable job skill on a résumé; 工艺 is a craft/manufacturing process. 技术 is the practical know-how itself.
collocations: 技术支持 (jìshù zhīchí) — technical support
高新技术 (gāoxīn jìshù) — high and new technology
技术含量 (jìshù hánliàng) — how much technical substance something has
sentence: 这家工厂引进了国外的先进技术。
sentence_meaning: This factory brought in advanced technology from abroad.

problem: Glossed with the bare verb 'compete', which sends you to 比赛; the noun use ('competition' as a market condition) is the more common one in writing and isn't shown.
meaning: Competition in the sense of rivalry — companies, candidates, or countries all going after the same thing. Used as both verb and noun, and mostly about economics, jobs and markets rather than sport.
contrast: 比赛 is an actual match or contest that gets played; 竞赛 is an organized contest (数学竞赛). 竞争 is the ongoing state of rivalry, with no fixed event.
collocations: 竞争对手 (jìngzhēng duìshǒu) — competitor, rival
竞争力 (jìngzhēnglì) — competitiveness
恶性竞争 (èxìng jìngzhēng) — cut-throat, destructive competition
sentence: 就业市场竞争激烈，很多毕业生选择继续读书。
sentence_meaning: Competition in the job market is fierce, so many graduates choose to keep studying.

problem: Tagged as a verb with the gloss '(make an) exception', but it's mainly a noun, and its commonest life is in fixed negative phrases — that's what should be memorized.
meaning: An exception to a rule. Most often you meet it in the negative: nobody is exempt, no exceptions, without exception.
contrast: 除外 means 'excluding' and goes after the excluded item (节假日除外); 特殊 means 'special'. 例外 is the exception itself, the case that breaks the rule.
collocations: 无一例外 (wúyī lìwài) — without a single exception
没有例外 (méiyǒu lìwài) — no exceptions
这次也不例外 (zhè cì yě bù lìwài) — this time is no different
sentence: 公司规定人人都要打卡，经理也不例外。
sentence_meaning: Company rules say everyone has to clock in — the manager included.

problem: 'Right; privilege' is fine but leaves the killer confusion untouched: 权利 vs 权力, identical in speech.
meaning: A right you're entitled to — legal or moral. It's the citizen's side of things and is almost always paired with 义务 (duties).
contrast: 权力 (same sound) is power/authority — what officials and institutions wield over others. 权利 is what you're owed; 权力 is what someone commands. 特权 is privilege proper.
collocations: 权利和义务 (quánlì hé yìwù) — rights and obligations
合法权利 (héfǎ quánlì) — legal rights
享有权利 (xiǎngyǒu quánlì) — to enjoy/hold a right
sentence: 消费者有权利要求退货，商家不能拒绝。
sentence_meaning: Consumers have the right to demand a refund, and merchants can't refuse.

problem: A one-word gloss with no hook — it's failing as an isolated label, not as a concept. Anchor it to the compounds it forms.
meaning: Chemistry, the school subject and the science; as a modifier, 'chemical'. Nearly all its everyday use is as the first half of 化学X.
collocations: 化学反应 (huàxué fǎnyìng) — chemical reaction
化学物质 (huàxué wùzhì) — chemical substance
化学武器 (huàxué wǔqì) — chemical weapons
sentence: 这两种液体混在一起会发生化学反应。
sentence_meaning: Mixing these two liquids will produce a chemical reaction.

problem: 'Theory' alone is hookless, and it hides the very common adverbial 理论上 as well as the unrelated verb sense.
meaning: A theory or body of doctrine — the systematic thinking behind a practice. Constantly set against 实践 (practice) and 实际 (reality).
contrast: 学说 is a named scholarly doctrine (进化学说); 道理 is a reason or common-sense point. Note also the separate verb 跟某人理论 = argue it out with someone, which trips people up.
collocations: 理论上 (lǐlùn shàng) — in theory, theoretically
理论与实践 (lǐlùn yǔ shíjiàn) — theory and practice
理论基础 (lǐlùn jīchǔ) — theoretical foundation
sentence: 理论上行得通，实际操作起来问题不少。
sentence_meaning: In theory it works, but in actual practice there are plenty of problems.

problem: The gloss is right but the card treats it as one solid verb; it's a verb-object pair that splits, and that's what makes it hard to produce.
meaning: To fall for a trick or scam — you took the bait. Spoken, everyday. Since 当 is the object, things go in between: 上了当, 上过好几次当, 上他的当.
contrast: 受骗 is the formal 'be deceived' you'd see in a news report; 吃亏 is losing out or getting the short end, with no trickery implied. 上当 always means somebody fooled you.
collocations: 上当受骗 (shàngdàng shòupiàn) — be taken in and cheated (set phrase)
别上当 (bié shàngdàng) — don't fall for it
上了他的当 (shàngle tā de dàng) — fell for his trick
sentence: 这种电话都是骗人的，千万别上当。
sentence_meaning: Calls like this are all scams — whatever you do, don't fall for it.
was: to be fooled; be taken in; be duped

problem: 'Member' overlaps with 会员/队员 and the card doesn't say which kind of group 成员 belongs to.
meaning: A member as a component part of a body — a family, a committee, a team, an organization, a country in an alliance. Slightly formal; it describes composition rather than joining.
contrast: 会员 is a paying/registered member of a club or website; 队员 is a team player; 委员 is a committee officeholder. 成员 is the neutral 'one of the people making up X'.
collocations: 家庭成员 (jiātíng chéngyuán) — family member
成员国 (chéngyuánguó) — member state
核心成员 (héxīn chéngyuán) — core member
sentence: 填表时要写清楚每位家庭成员的职业。
sentence_meaning: When filling in the form, state each family member's occupation clearly.
was: member (of a group, team, or family)

problem: Concrete and easy in isolation, which is probably why it slides off — nothing distinguishes it. Give it its metaphorical and sporting uses to make it stick.
meaning: A seed. Also used figuratively for the seed of something planted in a person, and in sports for a seeded player.
collocations: 种子选手 (zhǒngzi xuǎnshǒu) — seeded player, top seed
埋下种子 (máixià zhǒngzi) — plant a seed (figurative)
种子发芽 (zhǒngzi fāyá) — the seed sprouts
sentence: 那次经历在他心里埋下了一颗种子。
sentence_meaning: That experience planted a seed in his mind.

problem: 'Evolve' in English is loose and often just means 'gradually change'; 进化 is narrower, which is why the card misleads.
meaning: Evolution in the biological sense — species developing over generations, with the implication of progress toward something better adapted. Also used jokingly of gadgets or people 'levelling up'.
contrast: 演变 is neutral gradual change over time (局势演变), no improvement implied; 发展 is development/growth; 升级 is upgrading a version. Don't use 进化 where you just mean things changed.
collocations: 进化论 (jìnhuàlùn) — the theory of evolution
不断进化 (búduàn jìnhuà) — continually evolving
进化过程 (jìnhuà guòchéng) — the evolutionary process
sentence: 达尔文的进化论彻底改变了人们对生命的看法。
sentence_meaning: Darwin's theory of evolution completely changed how people saw life.

problem: Glossed as an abbreviation pair (AD/CE) with no sense of when a Chinese speaker actually says it — that's the missing piece.
meaning: The Common Era marker used before a year when dating history: 公元前 = BC, 公元 = AD. You only use it for historical dates far from the present; nobody says 公元2024年 in ordinary talk.
contrast: 世纪 is 'century' and often follows it (公元前三世纪); 年代 is a decade or era. 公元 fixes which side of year zero you're on.
collocations: 公元前 (gōngyuánqián) — BC/BCE
公元二世纪 (gōngyuán èr shìjì) — the 2nd century AD
公元1000年 (gōngyuán yīqiān nián) — the year 1000 AD
sentence: 孔子大约生活在公元前六世纪。
sentence_meaning: Confucius lived roughly in the 6th century BC.
was: AD; CE (Common Era); 公元前 = BC/BCE

problem: 'Analyze/analysis' is correct but weightless; the card gives no phrases, and the old sentence (doing a chemical analysis) is an odd, narrow use.
meaning: To break a situation down and work out what's going on, and the write-up that results. Used for problems, data, situations, markets — a standard word in reports and commentary.
contrast: 研究 is to research or study something over time; 解释 explains why to someone else. 分析 is the taking-apart itself, which may stay in your head.
collocations: 分析问题 (fēnxī wèntí) — analyze a problem
数据分析 (shùjù fēnxī) — data analysis
具体问题具体分析 (jùtǐ wèntí jùtǐ fēnxī) — analyze each case on its own terms
sentence: 专家分析，房价短期内不会大幅下跌。
sentence_meaning: Experts' analysis is that housing prices won't fall sharply in the short term.

problem: 'System; institution' is exactly the gloss shared by 系统, 体制 and 体系, so the card can't distinguish them.
meaning: A system of established rules — the written regulations an organization runs on, or the fundamental order of a society. If it's rules people must follow, it's 制度.
contrast: 系统 is a technical or connected system (操作系统, 神经系统); 体系 is a system of interrelated parts (法律体系); 体制 is the structural setup of a state or sector (教育体制). 制度 is specifically rules and institutional arrangements.
collocations: 管理制度 (guǎnlǐ zhìdù) — management rules/regulations
社会制度 (shèhuì zhìdù) — social system
制度改革 (zhìdù gǎigé) — institutional reform
sentence: 公司要建立一套完善的考勤制度。
sentence_meaning: The company needs to set up a proper attendance system.

problem: 'To explain' is shared with 说明 and 讲解, and the card omits the very common noun use ('an explanation' you owe someone).
meaning: To explain or account for something — to make a meaning clear, or to justify yourself when something looks bad. Also the noun: an explanation, an interpretation.
contrast: 说明 explains how something works or states facts (说明书, 说明情况); 讲解 is walking an audience through material; 辩解 is making excuses. 解释 covers both clarifying a meaning and defending your actions.
collocations: 做出解释 (zuòchū jiěshì) — give an explanation
解释原因 (jiěshì yuányīn) — explain the reason
最终解释权 (zuìzhōng jiěshìquán) — the right of final interpretation (in fine print)
sentence: 事故发生后，公司一直没有给出合理的解释。
sentence_meaning: Since the accident, the company still hasn't given a reasonable explanation.

problem: "Area/region/district" collapses it into 地区/范围, so nothing tells him which word to reach for.
meaning: A zone marked off for some purpose — a piece of space with a boundary and a function (parking zone, service zone, no-smoking zone). Also the formal word for "regional" in policy talk: 区域经济, 区域合作.
contrast: 地区 is a geographic/administrative region on the map (华北地区); 范围 is an abstract scope or extent (工作范围); 区域 is a delimited zone or slice of space, more technical.
collocations: 区域经济 (qūyù jīngjì) — regional economy
禁止吸烟区域 (jìnzhǐ xīyān qūyù) — no-smoking zone
划分区域 (huàfēn qūyù) — divide into zones
沿海区域 (yánhǎi qūyù) — the coastal zone
sentence: 公司把销售市场划分成五个区域。
sentence_meaning: The company divided the sales market into five zones.

problem: Three glosses (actual/reality/practice) with no sense of use; it also gets mixed up with 事实.
meaning: "Actual" as opposed to nominal, theoretical or planned — 实际情况, 实际收入. As a noun it's the real situation on the ground: 符合实际, 从实际出发. 实际上 = "actually, in fact".
contrast: 事实 is a single fact you can state or prove; 实际 is the practical reality versus the theory or the plan. 现实 is reality as harsh circumstances.
collocations: 实际情况 (shíjì qíngkuàng) — the actual situation
实际上 (shíjìshàng) — actually, in fact
不切实际 (bù qiè shíjì) — unrealistic, impractical
实际行动 (shíjì xíngdòng) — concrete action
sentence: 计划听起来不错，但不太符合实际。
sentence_meaning: The plan sounds fine, but it doesn't really fit the actual situation.

problem: Glossed like 继续, so he can't tell which to use; the card gives no sense of what kind of subject it takes.
meaning: Something goes on without a break over a stretch of time — a process, a state, weather, prices, growth. Written/news register, and it's usually the situation, not a person, that 持续s.
contrast: 继续 = a person carries on doing something (继续工作); 持续 = a condition keeps holding (高温持续). 连续 counts consecutive instances (连续三天下雨).
collocations: 持续增长 (chíxù zēngzhǎng) — sustained growth
持续了三个小时 (chíxù le sān ge xiǎoshí) — lasted three hours
可持续发展 (kě chíxù fāzhǎn) — sustainable development
持续高温 (chíxù gāowēn) — an ongoing heat wave
sentence: 这场谈判持续了将近五个小时。
sentence_meaning: The negotiation went on for nearly five hours.

problem: "(Surface) area" is right but sits next to 区域 in his head; nothing shows it's a measured quantity.
meaning: Size measured in square units — the number you get in 平方米. It's a quantity, so it takes 是/有/达 plus a figure, never a place you can stand in.
contrast: 区域 is a zone (a place); 面积 is how big it is (a number). 体积 is volume.
collocations: 建筑面积 (jiànzhù miànjī) — floor/built area
面积达…平方公里 (miànjī dá … píngfāng gōnglǐ) — covers … square km
扩大面积 (kuòdà miànjī) — enlarge the area
森林覆盖面积 (sēnlín fùgài miànjī) — forest coverage area
sentence: 这套房子的建筑面积有九十多平方米。
sentence_meaning: This apartment has a floor area of just over ninety square metres.

problem: "Be located at" doesn't say that it's a written-only verb with its own grammar, which is why it won't come to mind.
meaning: Written/formal "is situated in" — used in descriptions of places, companies, buildings. It swallows the 在: 位于市中心, never 位于在. No 了/着/过, no negation in practice.
contrast: 在 is the everyday word in speech; 处于 is for abstract states (处于困境); 坐落于 is for buildings specifically.
collocations: 位于市中心 (wèiyú shìzhōngxīn) — located downtown
位于…以南 (wèiyú … yǐnán) — situated to the south of…
总部位于 (zǒngbù wèiyú) — headquartered in
位于世界前列 (wèiyú shìjiè qiánliè) — ranks among the world's foremost
sentence: 该公司总部位于上海浦东。
sentence_meaning: The company's headquarters is in Pudong, Shanghai.

problem: "Fact; in fact" mashes the noun and 事实上 together and leaves it indistinguishable from 实际/真相.
meaning: A fact — something that is so and can be pointed to or proven. Lives in a small set of set phrases: 事实上, 事实证明, 摆事实讲道理.
contrast: 实际 is practical reality versus theory; 真相 is the hidden truth behind an event; 事实 is a verifiable item of fact you cite in an argument.
collocations: 事实上 (shìshíshàng) — in fact, as a matter of fact
事实证明 (shìshí zhèngmíng) — the facts prove that…
不符合事实 (bù fúhé shìshí) — not consistent with the facts
既成事实 (jìchéng shìshí) — a fait accompli
sentence: 他嘴上说不在意，事实上非常生气。
sentence_meaning: He says he doesn't care, but in fact he's furious.

problem: Listing it as "error; mistake; mistaken" hides that it's the formal noun and can't replace 错 as a predicate.
meaning: A mistake, as a countable formal noun: 犯错误, 改正错误, 语法错误. Used as a modifier it needs 的 — 错误的决定 "a wrong decision".
contrast: 错 is the everyday predicate (你错了 / 这个字写错了) — you can't say 你错误了. 失误 is a slip in performance (操作失误); 过错 is fault/blame.
collocations: 犯错误 (fàn cuòwù) — make a mistake
改正错误 (gǎizhèng cuòwù) — correct a mistake
错误的决定 (cuòwù de juédìng) — a wrong decision
拼写错误 (pīnxiě cuòwù) — spelling error
sentence: 年轻人犯点错误是难免的，重要的是改正。
sentence_meaning: It's inevitable that young people make some mistakes; what matters is fixing them.

problem: It's a fine standalone word, but the gloss "short; low" lets 短 and 低 leak in.
meaning: Low in height — people, trees, walls, furniture, buildings. The opposite of 高, and used bare as a predicate: 他很矮。
contrast: 短 is short in length (头发短, 裤子短); 低 is low in position or level (低价, 低声, 温度低). Height of a person or thing standing up = 矮.
collocations: 矮个子 (ǎi gèzi) — a short person
比我矮 (bǐ wǒ ǎi) — shorter than me
矮墙 (ǎi qiáng) — a low wall
矮小 (ǎixiǎo) — short and slight
sentence: 他比哥哥矮半个头。
sentence_meaning: He's half a head shorter than his older brother.

problem: "Apart from / except for" makes it look like a standalone conjunction; in fact it's a tail that clamps onto a noun phrase, and half its uses are literally "outside of".
meaning: Goes after a noun or phrase to mark "outside that boundary": physically or in time (三米以外, 一年以外), or "other than that" — usually paired up as 除了…以外. The clause after it typically has 还/也/都 or a negative.
contrast: 之外 is the same job in more literary writing; 以内/之内 is the inside counterpart. 除了 alone can't do it — the 以外 closes the bracket. 另外 starts a new sentence ("besides, …"), 以外 never does.
collocations: 除了…以外 (chúle … yǐwài) — apart from …
工作以外 (gōngzuò yǐwài) — outside of work
除此以外 (chú cǐ yǐwài) — apart from this
一公里以外 (yī gōnglǐ yǐwài) — more than a kilometre away
sentence: 除了签名以外，还需要盖公司的章。
sentence_meaning: Besides the signature, the company seal is also required.
was: Apart from, other than, except for

problem: "Disturb" doesn't capture that it's mostly a politeness formula, and it blurs into 麻烦.
meaning: To break in on someone who is busy or at peace. Its commonest life is as an apology when you interrupt: 打扰一下 / 不好意思，打扰了。
contrast: 麻烦你 asks someone to do work for you; 打扰 just intrudes on their time or quiet. 干扰 is technical interference (信号干扰); 妨碍 is obstructing.
collocations: 打扰一下 (dǎrǎo yíxià) — excuse me, sorry to bother you
打扰您了 (dǎrǎo nín le) — sorry to have troubled you
不想打扰他 (bù xiǎng dǎrǎo tā) — don't want to disturb him
别打扰他休息 (bié dǎrǎo tā xiūxi) — don't disturb his rest
sentence: 不好意思，打扰您一下，请问王老师在吗？
sentence_meaning: Sorry to bother you — is Teacher Wang in?

problem: The gloss is garbled ("to escapewithout") and mixes three senses without saying which objects go with which.
meaning: Standalone verb: take off clothing or shoes (脱衣服, 脱鞋, 脱下外套). Second sense: something comes off or falls out by itself — 脱皮, 脱发, 脱色. In compounds it's "break away from": 脱离, 逃脱, 摆脱.
contrast: 摘 is for things you unhook or remove from your head/hands — 摘帽子, 摘眼镜, 摘戒指. Clothes and shoes take 脱; the opposite is 穿.
collocations: 脱鞋 (tuō xié) — take off one's shoes
脱下外套 (tuōxià wàitào) — take off a coat
脱不开身 (tuō bu kāi shēn) — can't get away (too tied up)
脱水 (tuōshuǐ) — dehydration; spin-dry
sentence: 进屋请先脱鞋。
sentence_meaning: Please take your shoes off before coming in.
was: to shed; take off; to escapewithout

problem: "Mistake" is the meaning it has inside 错误/失误, not what it does standing alone; and the sentence is an anime line about 失误, not 误.
meaning: On its own it's a verb: to miss something because of a delay, or to hold something up — 误了火车, 别误了正事. As a prefix in compounds it means "by mistake, in error": 误伤, 误认为, 误会.
contrast: 耽误 is the everyday two-syllable verb for causing a delay; bare 误 is terser and more written. The noun "a mistake" is 错误/失误, not 误 alone.
collocations: 误了火车 (wù le huǒchē) — missed the train
误伤 (wùshāng) — injure by accident
误以为 (wù yǐwéi) — mistakenly think that
延误 (yánwù) — delay (of a flight, etc.)
sentence: 快走吧，别误了火车。
sentence_meaning: Let's get going, or we'll miss the train.
study_instead: 耽误 (dānwu) — to delay, hold up

problem: It isn't a word by itself in modern Chinese, so "to permit" is a meaning that never surfaces on its own — and there's no example sentence at all.
meaning: Background meaning: to consent, to grant. In practice you only ever meet it inside 允许 (permit, allow) and the more literary 允诺 (give one's promise), 应允 (assent).
contrast: 允许 is permission granted by a person, rule or authority; 答应 is agreeing to someone's request; 准许 is stiffer, official approval.
collocations: 允许 (yǔnxǔ) — to permit, allow
不允许 (bù yǔnxǔ) — not allowed
允诺 (yǔnnuò) — to promise, give one's word
默许 (mòxǔ) — tacit consent
sentence: 馆内不允许拍照。
sentence_meaning: Photography is not allowed inside the museum.

problem: "Key" is dangerously ambiguous — it isn't a door key and it isn't "key = crucial"; the sentence is a game fragment that teaches nothing.
meaning: A key you press: on a keyboard, a phone, a piano. It normally carries a modifier — 回车键, 空格键, 快捷键 — and lives in 键盘 and 按键.
contrast: 钥匙 is a key for a lock; 关键 is "key/crucial". 琴键 are piano keys.
collocations: 键盘 (jiànpán) — keyboard
按键 (ànjiàn) — button, keypress
快捷键 (kuàijiéjiàn) — keyboard shortcut
回车键 (huíchējiàn) — the Enter key
sentence: 输入完密码后请按回车键确认。
sentence_meaning: After entering your password, press Enter to confirm.

problem: He already knows "easy"; what he keeps missing is the second, commoner-in-writing use — "tends to, is prone to".
meaning: Easy to do (这道题很容易). But before a verb it means "readily happens / is liable to": 容易出错, 容易生锈, 容易被误解 — often about something unwanted.
contrast: 简单 is simple in structure or content, not effort; 轻松 is relaxed, low-strain. For "prone to", 容易 is the neutral word and 易 the written short form (易碎, 易燃).
collocations: 不容易 (bù róngyì) — not easy; no mean feat
容易出错 (róngyì chūcuò) — error-prone
很容易被误解 (hěn róngyì bèi wùjiě) — easily misunderstood
来得容易 (lái de róngyì) — comes easily
sentence: 这种材料很容易生锈，要放在干燥的地方。
sentence_meaning: This material rusts easily, so keep it somewhere dry.

problem: The card lists it as an adjective and misses that its most frequent use is the polite verb 麻烦你…
meaning: A hassle: as a noun (给你添麻烦了), as an adjective for a procedure that's fiddly (手续很麻烦), and as a verb for imposing on someone — 麻烦你帮我看一下, which is the standard polite way to ask a favour.
contrast: 打扰 is intruding on someone's time or quiet; 麻烦 is putting work on them. 困难 is genuine difficulty, not annoying fuss.
collocations: 麻烦你了 (máfan nǐ le) — sorry to put you to the trouble
添麻烦 (tiān máfan) — cause someone bother
怕麻烦 (pà máfan) — can't be bothered
手续很麻烦 (shǒuxù hěn máfan) — the procedure is a hassle
sentence: 麻烦你把这份文件转给王经理。
sentence_meaning: Could I trouble you to pass this document on to Manager Wang?

problem: A four-part gloss with no anchor; the real issue is telling it apart from 体验 and 理解.
meaning: To come to feel and understand something because you've lived it — usually someone's hardship, effort or feelings. Also a noun: the insight you took away (谈谈自己的体会, 心得体会).
contrast: 体验 is going through the experience itself (体验生活); 体会 is the understanding that experience leaves you with. 理解 is understanding by reasoning, no personal experience needed.
collocations: 深有体会 (shēn yǒu tǐhuì) — to know this all too well
体会到 (tǐhuì dào) — come to appreciate that…
亲身体会 (qīnshēn tǐhuì) — first-hand experience of it
谈谈体会 (tántan tǐhuì) — share what one has taken away
sentence: 自己当了父母，才真正体会到父母的辛苦。
sentence_meaning: Only after becoming a parent yourself do you really appreciate how hard your parents worked.
was: to know from experience; to realize; to understand; understanding gained from experience

problem: The two characters read as the verb pair "open and close", so the noun meaning slips away; the card gives no phrases to hang it on.
meaning: A switch — the physical thing you flip or press to cut power on and off. Always a noun, always with 按/开/关/坏 around it.
contrast: 按钮 is a button on a device or screen; 插头/插座 are plug and socket; 阀门 is a valve for water or gas. 开关 is specifically the on-off control.
collocations: 电源开关 (diànyuán kāiguān) — power switch
总开关 (zǒng kāiguān) — main switch, master breaker
按一下开关 (àn yíxià kāiguān) — press the switch
开关坏了 (kāiguān huài le) — the switch is broken
sentence: 走的时候记得把总开关关掉。
sentence_meaning: Remember to turn off the main switch when you leave.

problem: Glossing it as "cultivate; develop" makes it interchangeable with 培养, which it isn't — it takes a very narrow set of objects.
meaning: To build up a habit or trait in yourself over time. The object is almost always 习惯, sometimes 性格/作风/风气 — 养成早睡的习惯.
contrast: 培养 takes people or abilities as its object (培养人才, 培养兴趣) and is done by someone to someone; 养成 is a habit taking root, usually your own. 形成 is neutral "take shape" for patterns and systems.
collocations: 养成习惯 (yǎngchéng xíguàn) — form a habit
养成好的作风 (yǎngchéng hǎo de zuòfēng) — develop good work habits
从小养成 (cóngxiǎo yǎngchéng) — acquired from childhood
养成依赖性 (yǎngchéng yīlàixìng) — develop a dependency
sentence: 他从小就养成了记笔记的习惯。
sentence_meaning: He got into the habit of taking notes when he was young.
was: to cultivate; to form (a habit); to develop

problem: "Grow up; mature" makes it look like a synonym of 长大 and hides the very common business/career use.
meaning: To grow into something better — a child growing up healthy, but equally a person developing through work, or a company or market expanding. Written and slightly positive in tone.
contrast: 长大 is plain physical growing up (spoken); 生长 is biological growth of plants and animals; 发展 is the development of an undertaking or situation. 成长 keeps a sense of a person or entity maturing.
collocations: 健康成长 (jiànkāng chéngzhǎng) — grow up healthy
成长过程 (chéngzhǎng guòchéng) — the process of growing up
成长为 (chéngzhǎng wéi) — grow into (a …)
快速成长的企业 (kuàisù chéngzhǎng de qǐyè) — a fast-growing company
sentence: 这几年他在工作中成长得很快。
sentence_meaning: He's grown a lot through his work these past few years.

problem: The gloss lists four English verbs and no clue when 利用 is the right one of the "use" words, so it collapses into 使用/运用.
meaning: To turn something that already exists to your advantage — resources, spare time, an opening, a loophole, a person. It carries the sense of "leverage / capitalize on", which is why it also slides into "exploit" when the object is a person or a position.
contrast: 使用 is plain operating of a tool or product (使用手机). 运用 is applying knowledge, skill or a method (运用理论). 利用 is exploiting an existing condition for gain, and only 利用 can sound predatory: 他利用了我.
collocations: 充分利用 (chōngfèn lìyòng) — make full use of
利用机会 (lìyòng jīhuì) — seize the chance
利用职权 (lìyòng zhíquán) — abuse one's authority
加以利用 (jiāyǐ lìyòng) — put to use (formal)
sentence: 我们应该充分利用现有的资源，而不是盲目扩建。
sentence_meaning: We should make full use of the resources we already have instead of expanding blindly.
was: to use; to make use of; to take advantage of; to exploit

problem: "Complete" is correct but weightless; the card gives no sense of what kinds of objects 完成 takes, and the sentence 工作完成了 could equally be 做完了.
meaning: To carry a task through to its finish — the formal, goal-oriented word. It wants an object that was assigned or planned: a task, a project, a quota, a degree.
contrast: 做完 is the everyday "finished doing it". 结束 means an event comes to an end (会议结束了), with no sense of achievement. 完成 always implies something was accomplished as intended.
collocations: 完成任务 (wánchéng rènwù) — complete the assignment
按时完成 (ànshí wánchéng) — finish on schedule
完成学业 (wánchéng xuéyè) — finish one's studies
顺利完成 (shùnlì wánchéng) — complete smoothly
sentence: 这项工程必须在年底前完成。
sentence_meaning: This project has to be completed before the end of the year.
was: to accomplish; to complete; to fulfill

problem: "Friendly" makes it sound like everyday warmth, so it gets mixed up with 热情/亲切; in fact 友好 is mostly the vocabulary of relations between groups and countries.
meaning: Describes a relationship or attitude as being on good terms — cordial, well-disposed. It is the standard word in diplomatic and institutional language, and with people it describes stance toward someone (对…友好) rather than personal warmth.
contrast: 热情 is warm and enthusiastic hospitality; 亲切 is kindly and approachable in manner. 友好 is cooler and more official: 中美友好, 友好协商.
collocations: 友好关系 (yǒuhǎo guānxì) — friendly relations
友好访问 (yǒuhǎo fǎngwèn) — goodwill visit
对…友好 (duì…yǒuhǎo) — be friendly toward…
友好协商 (yǒuhǎo xiéshāng) — amicable consultation
sentence: 两国在会谈中同意进一步发展友好关系。
sentence_meaning: In the talks the two countries agreed to further develop friendly relations.

problem: Glossed identically to 为什么, so nothing on the card tells him when it would be used — and it is not really a spoken word.
meaning: The written-style "why". Same slot as 为什么 (before the verb), but it belongs in essays, news, and literary or rhetorical questions rather than conversation.
contrast: 为什么 is the neutral spoken form. 何故 is even more archaic. 怎么 asks "how come" with a note of surprise. Use 为何 when the register is formal or the question is rhetorical, and note the very common 不知为何 "for some reason".
collocations: 为何不 (wèihé bù) — why not…
不知为何 (bùzhī wèihé) — for some unknown reason
究竟为何 (jiūjìng wèihé) — why on earth
sentence: 不知为何，他这几天一直没有回复邮件。
sentence_meaning: For some reason he hasn't replied to any emails these past few days.

problem: Glossing it "opportunity" makes it interchangeable with 机会, which it isn't — 时机 is about timing, not about the opening itself.
meaning: The right moment, the timing of an action. You don't get a 时机 offered to you the way you get a 机会; you wait for it, judge it, and grab it when conditions ripen.
contrast: 机会 is a chance to do something (有机会去北京). 时机 asks whether now is the moment: 机会来了 vs 时机成熟了. You can't say 我有一个时机.
collocations: 时机成熟 (shíjī chéngshú) — the time is ripe
抓住时机 (zhuāzhù shíjī) — seize the moment
等待时机 (děngdài shíjī) — bide one's time
错过时机 (cuòguò shíjī) — miss the moment
sentence: 现在宣布还不合适，时机还不成熟。
sentence_meaning: Announcing it now isn't right — the time isn't ripe yet.

problem: "To come from (a place)" is too narrow and doesn't flag that this is the bookish form that takes its object directly, with no 从.
meaning: A written-style verb meaning "originates from": it attaches straight to the source, which can be a place, an institution, or an abstract source like pressure, funding, or data.
contrast: Spoken Chinese says 他从法国来 or 他是法国人; 来自 is what you see in introductions, reports and captions. Don't add 从 — 来自法国, not 从来自法国.
collocations: 来自世界各地 (láizì shìjiè gèdì) — from all over the world
数据来自 (shùjù láizì) — the data comes from
压力来自 (yālì láizì) — the pressure comes from
来自民间 (láizì mínjiān) — grassroots in origin
sentence: 本次论坛的与会者来自二十多个国家。
sentence_meaning: The participants in this forum come from more than twenty countries.

problem: Tagging it a pronoun is misleading — it is not a substitute for 自己. You cannot say 他只关心自我 in place of 自己.
meaning: A bound element meaning "self-" that sits in front of a two-syllable verb: 自我介绍, 自我批评. As a noun it means the ego/the self, and then it appears in fixed psychological phrases.
contrast: 自己 is the real reflexive pronoun and does all ordinary work (我自己做, 他自己的车). 自我 only forms compounds; if the sentence needs "myself/himself" as an object, it's 自己.
collocations: 自我介绍 (zìwǒ jièshào) — introduce oneself
自我批评 (zìwǒ pīpíng) — self-criticism
自我控制 (zìwǒ kòngzhì) — self-control
以自我为中心 (yǐ zìwǒ wéi zhōngxīn) — self-centred
sentence: 他做事完全以自我为中心，很少考虑别人。
sentence_meaning: He is completely self-centred in what he does and rarely considers others.

problem: Three glosses pointing three ways ("setback / defeat / frustration") blur it into 失败 and 困难.
meaning: A setback — you were pushing toward something and got knocked back. It names the blow to your effort and morale, so it goes with verbs of suffering and with 感 for the resulting feeling.
contrast: 失败 is the failed outcome itself (考试失败). 困难 is a difficulty standing in your way. 挫折 is the experience of being thwarted along the way: 遭受挫折 is standard, 遭受失败 is not.
collocations: 遭受挫折 (zāoshòu cuòzhé) — suffer a setback
受到挫折 (shòudào cuòzhé) — meet with a setback
挫折感 (cuòzhégǎn) — sense of frustration
经受挫折 (jīngshòu cuòzhé) — go through setbacks
sentence: 他在创业初期遭受过不少挫折，但从没想过放弃。
sentence_meaning: He suffered quite a few setbacks in the early days of his business, but never thought of giving up.

problem: "Comprise / consist of" is misleading: 包括 lists some of the members, it does not equal the whole. And the card doesn't show the 包括…在内 frame.
meaning: To include, i.e. to have something among its members. Typically a whole followed by examples, or negated to mark exclusions; with a person or item you often wrap it as 包括…在内.
contrast: 包含 is for something contained inside as content or implication (这句话包含另一层意思). 由…组成 is the one that means "consists of" exhaustively. 包括 just points at items on the list.
collocations: 包括…在内 (bāokuò…zàinèi) — including …
不包括 (bù bāokuò) — not including
包括在内的 (…) 费用 — costs included
其中包括 (qízhōng bāokuò) — among which are
sentence: 报价包括住宿和早餐，但不包括机票。
sentence_meaning: The quoted price includes lodging and breakfast but not airfare.

problem: "Even" is shared with 连…都 and 就连, and "so much so that" is really 以至于 — the card mixes two different words.
meaning: Escalation marker: after saying something, it introduces the most extreme case, the one that proves the point. It sits right before that extreme item, and very often pairs with 连…都/也.
contrast: 而且 merely adds another item at the same level; 甚至 must go further than what came before. 以至于 introduces a resulting consequence, not a stronger example. 连…都 can stand alone, but 甚至连…都 is the usual combination.
collocations: 甚至连…都 (shènzhì lián…dōu) — even …
甚至可以说 (shènzhì kěyǐ shuō) — one could even say
甚至更 (shènzhì gèng) — even more so
sentence: 这本书写得太专业，甚至连业内人士都看不懂。
sentence_meaning: The book is written so technically that even people in the field can't understand it.
was: even (to the point of); so much so that

problem: "Structure; composition" is correct but attached to nothing, so it never comes to mind in the contexts where Chinese actually uses it.
meaning: How the parts of something are arranged — a building's framework, a sentence's grammar, an economy's makeup. It is the word you reach for when talking about arrangement that can be analyzed or reorganized.
contrast: 构成 is a verb, "be made up of", or the makeup as a list of components. 组织 is the organization as a body. 结构 is the shape of the arrangement itself: 调整结构 means restructuring.
collocations: 句子结构 (jùzi jiégòu) — sentence structure
组织结构 (zǔzhī jiégòu) — organizational structure
产业结构 (chǎnyè jiégòu) — industrial structure
结构合理 (jiégòu hélǐ) — well-structured
sentence: 政府近年来一直在调整产业结构。
sentence_meaning: In recent years the government has been adjusting the industrial structure.

problem: "Community" in English covers everything from a neighborhood to an online forum to an ethnic group; the card doesn't say which sense 社区 has.
meaning: A neighborhood treated as a unit with services and administration — the level below a district, with its own office, clinic, activity center. By extension it also names online communities.
contrast: 小区 is just the physical residential compound you live in. 团体 is an organized group. 社区 is the neighborhood as a social/administrative entity: 社区医院, 社区工作者.
collocations: 社区服务 (shèqū fúwù) — community services
社区居民 (shèqū jūmín) — community residents
社区活动 (shèqū huódòng) — community activities
网络社区 (wǎngluò shèqū) — online community
sentence: 社区为老年人提供免费体检和送餐服务。
sentence_meaning: The community provides free health checks and meal delivery for the elderly.

problem: "Resident; inhabitant" doesn't distinguish it from 公民 or 住户, and the sentence 他是本地居民 shows nothing about how it's normally used.
meaning: The people who live in a place, seen collectively — the word used in news and notices when talking about how something affects the people living there. Almost always preceded by the place: 当地居民, 城市居民.
contrast: 公民 is citizen, a legal status. 人口 is population as a number. 住户 is households in a building. 居民 is simply the people who live somewhere, and it is the word officials use about them.
collocations: 当地居民 (dāngdì jūmín) — local residents
居民区 (jūmínqū) — residential area
城市居民 (chéngshì jūmín) — urban residents
居民收入 (jūmín shōurù) — household income
sentence: 附近的居民联名反对在这里建垃圾站。
sentence_meaning: Residents nearby signed a joint petition against building a garbage station here.

problem: Glossing it "person" invites him to use it like 人, but 人士 never stands alone — it only appears after a modifier and is a respectful, formal label.
meaning: A polite formal word for people of a specified category, used in news and official writing. It always follows a descriptor — which field they're from, how prominent they are, what group they belong to.
contrast: 人员 is staff/personnel doing a job (工作人员). 人物 is a notable figure or a character in a story. 人士 is respectful reference to people of a stated category, and 各界人士 is its most typical shape.
collocations: 各界人士 (gèjiè rénshì) — people from all walks of life
知名人士 (zhīmíng rénshì) — well-known figures
专业人士 (zhuānyè rénshì) — professionals
有关人士 (yǒuguān rénshì) — people concerned
sentence: 开幕式邀请了社会各界人士出席。
sentence_meaning: People from all walks of life were invited to attend the opening ceremony.

problem: The four glosses mix noun and verb and don't separate it from 贸易 or 买卖; the sample sentence only teaches the compound 交易所.
meaning: A deal — one exchange in which goods, shares or money change hands. Used for concrete business transactions, and figuratively for a shady bargain between parties.
contrast: 贸易 is trade as an economic activity between countries or sectors (国际贸易). 买卖 is buying and selling as a small business. 交易 is the individual transaction: 达成一笔交易.
collocations: 达成交易 (dáchéng jiāoyì) — strike a deal
进行交易 (jìnxíng jiāoyì) — carry out a transaction
交易额 (jiāoyì'é) — transaction volume
内幕交易 (nèimù jiāoyì) — insider trading
sentence: 双方经过几轮谈判，终于达成了交易。
sentence_meaning: After several rounds of negotiation the two sides finally struck a deal.
was: transaction; deal; trade; to do business

problem: "Scale; scope; extent" runs it together with 范围 and 程度; nothing on the card says it's about the size of an undertaking.
meaning: How big an operation, project or event is — headcount, output, floor space, reach all rolled into one. It's the word for whether a business, a war, a protest or a factory is big or small.
contrast: 范围 is the range something covers (活动范围, 范围很广). 程度 is degree of intensity. 规模 is sheer size of an enterprise or undertaking: 大规模生产, 规模不大.
collocations: 扩大规模 (kuòdà guīmó) — expand the scale
大规模 (dàguīmó) — large-scale
规模空前 (guīmó kōngqián) — unprecedented in scale
生产规模 (shēngchǎn guīmó) — production scale
sentence: 这家企业规模不大，但技术很有竞争力。
sentence_meaning: This company isn't large, but its technology is quite competitive.

problem: Putting "consider; believe" alongside "(mistakenly)" hides the one thing that matters: 以为 signals the belief turned out to be wrong.
meaning: To have thought something that wasn't so. Saying 我以为… already announces that reality was different, which is why it's usually about the past and often followed by 其实 or 原来.
contrast: 认为 states an opinion you still hold, neutrally and somewhat formally; 觉得 is the casual "feel/think". Swap 以为 in and you've admitted a mistake. (The formal 以…为… "regard as" is a separate pattern.)
collocations: 我以为…原来 (wǒ yǐwéi…yuánlái) — I thought … but actually
还以为 (hái yǐwéi) — I even thought
误以为 (wù yǐwéi) — mistakenly assume
sentence: 我以为今天不用上班，原来是我把日子记错了。
sentence_meaning: I thought I didn't have to work today — turns out I had the date wrong.

problem: "Especially; particularly" is exactly the gloss of 特别, so the card can't tell him which to use.
meaning: Singles out the standout case from something you have just stated in general terms. It needs that general statement first, and then usually comes as 尤其是 + the item.
contrast: 特别 also means "especially", but it doubles as "special/unusual" and as an intensifier (特别冷 = very cold); 尤其 only does the singling-out job and is more written. 尤其 cannot simply mean "very".
collocations: 尤其是 (yóuqí shì) — especially
尤其重要 (yóuqí zhòngyào) — particularly important
尤其明显 (yóuqí míngxiǎn) — particularly obvious
sentence: 南方的夏天很潮湿，尤其是梅雨季节。
sentence_meaning: Summers in the south are very humid, especially during the plum-rain season.

problem: "To defeat, to beat" leaves the direction ambiguous — the trap is that 败 alone means to lose, so he hesitates over who won.
meaning: A打败B means A wins and B is beaten; the object is always the opponent, never the match. Colloquial and everyday, used for games, matches, elections, fights.
contrast: 战胜 is the formal version and can also take abstract enemies (战胜困难). 打赢 takes the contest as object (打赢这场比赛). Bare 败 means to be defeated: 我们队败了 = we lost.
collocations: 打败对手 (dǎbài duìshǒu) — beat the opponent
被…打败 (bèi…dǎbài) — be defeated by
轻松打败 (qīngsōng dǎbài) — beat easily
sentence: 我们队在决赛中打败了上届冠军。
sentence_meaning: Our team beat the defending champions in the final.

problem: The card lumps two uses together with no example of either, and 意外事件发生了 is stiff, textbook-sounding Chinese.
meaning: Two jobs. As a feeling/quality: unexpected, surprising — 感到意外, 意外的消息. As a noun: a mishap or accident, the unlucky event nobody planned for.
contrast: 事故 is the formal word for an accident with damage (交通事故) and never means "surprised". 惊讶 is only the emotion of surprise. 意外 covers both the surprise and the unfortunate event.
collocations: 感到意外 (gǎndào yìwài) — be surprised
出乎意外 (chūhū yìwài) — contrary to expectations
意外收获 (yìwài shōuhuò) — unexpected bonus
发生意外 (fāshēng yìwài) — an accident happens
sentence: 他突然辞职的消息让同事们都很意外。
sentence_meaning: The news that he suddenly resigned came as a surprise to his colleagues.

problem: The gloss is right but the tag "verb with nominal function" is confusing, and the sentence only shows it buried inside 游泳池, where it isn't doing anything.
meaning: To swim — literally 游 (move through water) + 泳 (swimming), so it's verb + object glued together. That's why you can split it: 游了一会儿泳, 游了两千米. It also works as a plain noun: 我最喜欢的运动是游泳.
contrast: Because 泳 is already the object, you don't say 游泳一个小时 in careful speech — you say 游一个小时(的)泳 or 游泳游了一个小时.
collocations: 游泳池 (yóuyǒngchí) — swimming pool
去游泳 (qù yóuyǒng) — go swimming
游泳比赛 (yóuyǒng bǐsài) — swimming competition
游泳衣 (yóuyǒngyī) — swimsuit
sentence: 他每周去游泳两次，一次游一千米。
sentence_meaning: He goes swimming twice a week, a thousand metres each time.

problem: "To act" is too narrow, and the anime sentence hides it inside 会演.
meaning: Stands alone fine as a verb: to perform, to play (a role), to be showing. 谁演的？这部戏演的是抗战时期的故事。In compounds it widens out to "unfold, work through step by step" — 演讲 (give a speech), 演变 (evolve), 演习 (drill), 演算 (work out a calculation).
contrast: 演 is performing/playing a part; 表演 is the performance as an act or event; 扮 (扮演) stresses dressing up as someone.
collocations: 演电影 / 演话剧 (yǎn diànyǐng / huàjù) — act in a film / stage play
主演 (zhǔyǎn) — star in, lead role
演讲 (yǎnjiǎng) — deliver a speech
演变 (yǎnbiàn) — evolve, develop over time
sentence: 这部电视剧他演一个乡村医生，演得很自然。
