sentence_meaning: In this TV series he plays a village doctor, and he plays it very naturally.

problem: "Code; number" describes 码 as a suffix, but the sentence uses the completely separate counter sense (一码事), so the card teaches two unconnected things without saying so.
meaning: Standalone it's (a) the unit "yard", and (b) the counter for matters in 一码事 / 两码事 — 这是两码事 "those are two different things". Everywhere else it's the "-number / -code" element on the end of a word.
contrast: 号码 is a number assigned to something (phone, room); 密码 is a secret code you type in; 代码 is code in the programming/symbolic sense.
collocations: 号码 (hàomǎ) — number (phone, license, etc.)
密码 (mìmǎ) — password, PIN
起码 (qǐmǎ) — at the very least
两码事 (liǎng mǎ shì) — two entirely different matters
sentence: 请输入手机号码和密码；顺便说一句，注册和付款是两码事。
sentence_meaning: Please enter your phone number and password; by the way, registering and paying are two separate matters.

problem: "To invite" is shared with 请, so nothing tells him when to reach for the two-character word; the passive sentence doesn't show it either.
meaning: The formal act of inviting someone — issuing an invitation, usually to an event, and usually with some ceremony. It's also a noun: 接受邀请, 应他的邀请.
contrast: 请 is everyday and can mean treating someone (请你吃饭); 邀请 is the official version — you 邀请 someone 参加婚礼/出席会议, and you never say 邀请你吃个饭 casually.
collocations: 邀请函 (yāoqǐnghán) — written invitation
接受邀请 (jiēshòu yāoqǐng) — accept an invitation
应…的邀请 (yìng…de yāoqǐng) — at the invitation of…
邀请赛 (yāoqǐngsài) — invitational tournament
sentence: 我们已经正式邀请他出席下个月的开幕式。
sentence_meaning: We have formally invited him to attend next month's opening ceremony.

problem: The gloss chain "abandon; renounce; give up" makes it look usable for abandoning people or objects, which it isn't.
meaning: To let go of something you have or could have — a chance, a right, a plan, an effort. The object is almost always abstract, and the decision is yours.
contrast: 抛弃/遗弃 is abandoning a person; 丢弃/扔 is throwing away an object; 放弃 is giving up a claim or an attempt.
collocations: 放弃机会 (fàngqì jīhuì) — give up an opportunity
放弃治疗 (fàngqì zhìliáo) — stop treatment
永不放弃 (yǒng bù fàngqì) — never give up
放弃权利 (fàngqì quánlì) — waive a right
sentence: 为了照顾家人，她放弃了出国留学的机会。
sentence_meaning: To look after her family, she gave up the chance to study abroad.

problem: Not a standalone word in modern Chinese — asking for its meaning alone asks for something that never comes up, and the anime 弃狗 isn't normal usage (you'd say 流浪狗 or 被遗弃的狗).
meaning: Written-style "cast off, discard". Useful only as a clue inside compounds: 弃权 (abstain / forfeit), 遗弃 (abandon a dependent), 嫌弃 (reject as unwanted), 自暴自弃 (give up on oneself).
collocations: 放弃 (fàngqì) — give up (a chance, a plan)
抛弃 (pāoqì) — abandon, cast aside (a person)
弃权 (qìquán) — abstain from voting; forfeit a match
sentence: 他因为受伤，最后一场比赛只好弃权。
sentence_meaning: Because of his injury he had to forfeit the last match.

problem: Two English nouns and no sentence at all — nothing to hang it on.
meaning: Stands alone as "a mine" (这座矿已经关了；下矿). As a word-part it means ore or mineral: the stuff in the ground and the place it's dug out of.
contrast: 矿 is the deposit or the pit; 矿石 is the ore rock itself; 矿工 is the miner.
collocations: 煤矿 (méikuàng) — coal mine
矿泉水 (kuàngquánshuǐ) — mineral water
矿产资源 (kuàngchǎn zīyuán) — mineral resources
采矿 (cǎikuàng) — to mine, mining
sentence: 这座煤矿已经开采了三十年，去年正式关闭。
sentence_meaning: This coal mine had been worked for thirty years and was officially closed last year.

problem: "Appraise; estimate" hides the commonest use: 估计 as a stand-alone "I reckon / probably" at the front of a sentence.
meaning: To size something up roughly. Two lives: the plain verb (估计损失/人数) and the everyday hedge at the head of a clause — 估计他不来了 "he's probably not coming".
contrast: 预计 is a formal projection of a figure or schedule (预计到达时间); 评估 is a proper evaluation or assessment (风险评估); 估计 is your own rough guess and can be spoken casually.
collocations: 据估计 (jù gūjì) — it is estimated that
初步估计 (chūbù gūjì) — a preliminary estimate
估计错了 (gūjì cuò le) — misjudged it
估计不足 (gūjì bùzú) — underestimated
sentence: 据初步估计，这次台风造成的损失超过一千万元。
sentence_meaning: According to preliminary estimates, the typhoon caused over ten million yuan in losses.

problem: "Miscellaneous" is a dictionary label, and the sentence is a game fragment (小杂兵) that doesn't show normal use.
meaning: Stands alone as an adjective: mixed, of all sorts, hence messy or impure. 他手上的事很杂；这批货品种太杂；声音很杂. Inside words it's the "assorted/mixed" element.
contrast: 乱 is disordered; 杂 is many different kinds thrown together — things can be 杂 without being 乱.
collocations: 复杂 (fùzá) — complicated
杂志 (zázhì) — magazine
杂货店 (záhuòdiàn) — general store
杂乱 (záluàn) — jumbled, in disarray
sentence: 他管的事太杂，什么都要过问，结果哪件都做不好。
sentence_meaning: He handles too many different things and has to weigh in on everything, so he does none of them well.

problem: Glossed as the noun "translation", but it's a verb, and there's no sentence.
meaning: To translate — used alone in written Chinese, especially on title pages and in publishing: 译成英文, 由李明译, 全书由他一人译出. The noun senses come from compounds.
contrast: 翻译 is the everyday word and also means "a translator/interpreter"; bare 译 is bookish and only ever the act of translating.
collocations: 译成英文 (yì chéng Yīngwén) — translate into English
译者 (yìzhě) — translator (of a text)
口译 / 笔译 (kǒuyì / bǐyì) — interpreting / written translation
直译 (zhíyì) — literal translation
sentence: 这本小说已经被译成十几种语言。
sentence_meaning: This novel has already been translated into more than a dozen languages.

problem: The three English verbs blur together, and the sentence is an anime line using a rare compound (突降).
meaning: Stands alone for a level going down, or for bringing one down: 物价降了, 水位降了两米, 气温一下降到零度. In compounds it's the "lower it" element — 降价, 降温, 降低. Note the second reading xiáng only in 投降 (surrender).
contrast: 降 is about levels and quantities (prices, temperature, altitude); 掉 is something physically falling off or dropping; 落 is landing or settling.
collocations: 降价 (jiàngjià) — cut the price
降温 (jiàngwēn) — temperature drop; cool down
下降 (xiàjiàng) — decline, go down
降落 (jiàngluò) — land (a plane)
sentence: 这两年房价降了不少，但成交量也跟着降下来了。

problem: "To wish (well)" is right but shapeless; the anime line doesn't show the frame the word actually lives in.
meaning: Stands alone, but essentially only in one pattern: 祝 + person + good thing. 祝你生日快乐, 祝大家新年快乐, 祝您身体健康. It's how you sign off a letter or raise a toast.
contrast: 祝 is offering a wish for the future; 祝贺/恭喜 is congratulating on something that already happened.

problem: Not a standalone word, and "to loathe" is too strong — 厌 is being fed up, not hating.
meaning: "Sick of, had enough of." Two places it shows up: in 讨厌 / 厌倦 / 厌烦, and in the pattern verb + 厌了 — 听厌了, 看厌了, 吃厌了 (which is exactly what the long passage was doing).
contrast: 恨 is hate; 厌 is weariness from too much of something.
collocations: 讨厌 (tǎoyàn) — to dislike, be annoying
厌倦 (yànjuàn) — be weary of, tired of

problem: Four adjectives in English, no word, no sentence — nothing to recall.
meaning: Filth and its verb, "to foul". Not used alone: it lives in 污染 (pollute), 污水 (waste water), 污点 (a stain, on cloth or on a record), and the "corrupt" sense in 贪污 (embezzle).

problem: The gloss "Humor" is simply wrong — that's 幽默's meaning, and 幽默 is a sound-borrowing of English "humour", so the characters contribute nothing. 幽 also isn't a word on its own.
meaning: Deep, dim, secluded, hushed — and by extension the world of the dead. It gives 幽静 (quiet and secluded), 幽暗 (dim), 幽灵 (ghost). Learn it via 幽默 as a set unit, and via 幽静 for the real meaning.
collocations: 幽默 (yōumò) — humour, humorous (phonetic loan; don't decompose it)

幽灵 (yōulíng) — ghost, spectre
幽暗 (yōu'àn) — dim, gloomy
